speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS)

Based on your history of taking haloperidol for tics, your fever without chills, and altered mental status, the combination of rigidity and fever is highly suggestive of a reaction to the medication rather than an infection. I need to confirm if you have noticed severe muscle stiffness or "lead-pipe" rigidity since the symptoms started. REQUEST TEST: Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel and CK_level.
